key_insight: A steric-engineered ternary-solvent strategy produces hybrid perovskite monolayers exceeding 1000 μm² in lateral area, enabling lithography-free, low-static-power optoelectronics.
engineering_relevance: Large ultrathin flakes support solvent-free shadow-mask contacts, avoiding lithography-related chemical degradation while enabling low-leakage planar devices.
method: Combine alcohol cosolvents with an amine additive to suppress out-of-plane stacking.
Use molecular dynamics and quantum-chemical calculations to explain solvation changes and sustained edge-mediated growth.
Fabricate isolated ultrathin perovskite channels using physical shadow masking.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports (PEA)₂CuCl₄ monolayers above 1000 μm² and ultrathin (PEA)₂PbI₄ devices with dark currents of 10⁻¹⁵–10⁻¹³ A, approximately 0.2 pW static power at 5 V, and a light-to-dark current ratio of 430.
watch_item: The abstract demonstrates optoelectronic channels, not solar-cell efficiency or AI methods; manufacturing yield and long-term stability remain unreported.
paper_title: Universal Synthesis of Large-Area Hybrid Perovskite Monolayers Enabling Lithography-Free, Low-Static-Power Optoelectronics
